drivingQuestion: May diners who are acquainted — two brothers who are particular about each other's food — eat meat and cheese at one table?
outcomeNote: Abaye's ruling stands: the laundering permission is distinguished, since the belt makes the ground of that exception evident to onlookers.

segments.he: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: שְׁנֵי אַכְסְנָאִים שֶׁנִּתְאָרְחוּ לְפוּנְדָּק אֶחָד, זֶה בָּא מִן הַצָּפוֹן וְזֶה בָּא מִן הַדָּרוֹם, זֶה בָּא בַּחֲתִיכָתוֹ וְזֶה בָּא בִּגְבִינָתוֹ, אוֹכְלִין עַל שֻׁלְחָן אֶחָד, זֶה בָּשָׂר וְזֶה גְּבִינָה, וְאֵין חוֹשְׁשִׁין.
segments.en: «That» opinion «is also taught» in a baraita: «Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:» If «two guests roomed in one inn, this one coming from the north and that one coming from the south, this one coming with his piece» of meat «and that one coming with his cheese, they may eat» together «on one table, this one» eating «meat and that one cheese, and they» need «not be concerned.»

segments.he: וְלֹא אָסְרוּ אֶלָּא בִּתְפִיסָה אַחַת. תְּפִיסָה אַחַת סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ? אֶלָּא כְּעֵין תְּפִיסָה אַחַת.
segments.en: The baraita adds: «And» the Sages «prohibited» this practice «only» if they both eat «from one parcel.» The Gemara adds: Can it «enter your mind» that the baraita is actually referring to a case where they eat from «one parcel?» This is obviously prohibited. «Rather,» it prohibits eating even in a manner «as though» they were eating from «one parcel,» i.e., when the diners are somewhat acquainted with each other, since neither would mind if the other ate from his food.

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יֵימַר בַּר שֶׁלֶמְיָא לְאַבָּיֵי: שְׁנֵי אַחִין, וּמַקְפִּידִין זֶה עַל זֶה, מַהוּ?
segments.en: § It was stated above that if two diners are acquainted with each other they may not eat meat and cheese on the same table. «Rav Yeimar bar Shelemya said to Abaye:» If these diners are «two brothers, but they are» each «particular» not to let «one another» eat of his food, «what is» the halakha? May they eat separate dishes of meat and cheese at a single table?

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: יֹאמְרוּ כׇּל הַסְּרִיקִין אֲסוּרִין, וּסְרִיקֵי בַיְיתּוֹס מוּתָּרִין?!
segments.en: Abaye «said to him:» Your question evokes that of Baitos ben Zunin. The Sages prohibited the baking of elaborately decorated Syrian cakes for Passover, lest people tarry in their preparation and the cakes become leavened. Baitos wished to prepare the cakes in a way that would not lead to a violation of any prohibition, and yet the Sages prohibited it, because people «will say: All the» decorated «Syrian cakes are forbidden, but the Syrian cakes of Baitos are permitted?» Here too, to avoid confusion, we will not allow exceptions to the rule.

segments.he: וּלְטַעְמָיךְ, הָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מִי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא חָלוּק אֶחָד מוּתָּר לְכַבְּסוֹ בְּחוּלּוֹ שֶׁל מוֹעֵד. יֹאמְרוּ:
segments.en: Rav Yeimar responded: «But according to your reasoning,» one may refute «that which Rabbi Asi said» that «Rabbi Yoḥanan said:» Although the Sages prohibited laundering on the intermediate days of a Festival, «one who has only one shirt is permitted to launder it on the intermediate days of a Festival.» Here too, one can claim: People «will say» metaphorically:

segments.he: כׇּל הַסְּרִיקִין אֲסוּרִין וּסְרִיקֵי בַיְיתּוֹס מוּתָּרִין? הָתָם, הָא אָמַר מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי: אֵיזוֹרוֹ מוֹכִיחַ עָלָיו.
segments.en: «All the Syrian cakes are prohibited, but the Syrian cakes of Baitos are permitted?» The Gemara responds: With regard to the case «there, Mar, son of Rav Ashi, said: His belt is proof for him,» as in those days people commonly had one belt, which was worn over the shirt. If a person had more than one shirt, then whenever he laundered one he would remove the belt and wear it over the second. If one saw a shirt being washed with its belt, he would know that the owner had only one shirt.

moves.summary: adduces a baraita of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel matching Shmuel's limitation stated in the preceding unit
moves.about: bringing a baraita of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel about two guests who lodged in one inn, one arriving from the north and one from the south

moves.summary: the baraita's closing clause: the Sages forbade only where the two eat from one parcel
moves.about: re-reading the baraita's one parcel as something like one parcel, i.e. diners acquainted enough that neither minds the other eating his food

moves.summary: the literal sense of one parcel would be obvious and could not be what the baraita teaches
moves.about: whether the baraita can really mean that only eating literally from one parcel was forbidden, which would be obvious

moves.summary: the baraita forbids even something like one parcel — diners familiar enough not to mind sharing

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה רב יימר בר שלמיא לאביי
moves.summary: asks Abaye whether two brothers who are particular about each other's food may share a table
moves.about: whether two brothers who are particular that the other not eat his food may eat meat and cheese at one table

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: יאמרו כל הסריקין אסורין
moves.summary: they too are forbidden, for the Sages do not permit an exception that will look inconsistent
moves.about: even particular brothers are forbidden, since the Sages carve no exceptions into a decree lest people say that all decorated cakes are forbidden but those of Baitos permitted

moves.summary: on that reasoning the accepted permission to launder one's only shirt on ḥol hamo'ed should also fall
moves.about: whether Abaye's people-will-say reasoning would not equally bar the permission for one who owns a single shirt to launder it on the intermediate days of a Festival

moves.cueHe: התם, הא אמר מר בר רב אשי
moves.summary: there the belt worn with the shirt makes the reason for the exception visible, so nothing looks inconsistent
moves.about: the laundering case is different, because the belt worn with the shirt shows onlookers that its owner has only one, so no inconsistency will be suspected
